title: なかなか — quite / (not) easily
summary: An adverb with two uses. With a positive word it means “quite, considerably, better than expected.” With a negative verb (なかなか〜ない) it means “not easily, takes a long time to happen.”

patterns.form: なかなか＋形容詞／動詞（肯定）

patterns.gloss: does not happen easily / takes a long time

body.p: Placed before an adjective or verb, it means the degree is higher than expected. In “this shop’s cake is なかなか good” it is an evaluation that usually carries some praise. Be careful when judging someone above you with it, as it can sound condescending.
When a negative form follows, it means “it does not go as hoped / it does not happen easily.” バスがなかなか来ない means you keep waiting and the bus will not come, with a hint of irritation.

examples.ja: この問題（もんだい）はなかなか難（むずか）しい。
examples.note: Positive use: the problem is harder than it looks.

examples.ja: この店（みせ）のケーキは、なかなかおいしい。
examples.romaji: Kono mise no kēki wa, nakanaka oishii.
examples.tr: The cake at this shop is quite good.
examples.note: Positive use with a pleasant surprise.

examples.ja: バスがなかなか来（こ）なくて、困（こま）ってしまった。
examples.romaji: Basu ga nakanaka konakute, komatte shimatta.
examples.tr: The bus just wouldn't come, and I was in trouble.
examples.note: なかなか + negative (来なくて) = “not easily / not for a long time.”

pitfalls: The meaning depends on whether a negative follows. なかなか〜ない means “not easily,” not “not very.”
Used as praise, it can sound condescending toward someone of higher status.
